'''Liv Hornekær''' (born 1972 in [[Copenhagen]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|title=Liv Hornekær — Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet|url=https://ufm.dk/forskning-og-innovation/forskningsformidling/eliteforsk/prismodtagere/tidligere-prismodtagere/prismodtagere-2016/eliteforsk-priserne-2016/liv-hornekaer|access-date=2021-09-21|website=ufm.dk|language=da}}</ref>) is a Danish experimental physicist who works in [[nanotechnology]] and [[Astrochemistry|astrochemical]] research.

She is a professor at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at [[Aarhus University]] and head of the surface dynamics group at the department.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|title=The group|url=https://phys.au.dk/forskning/forskningsomraader/condensed-matter-physics/surface-dynamics-group/the-group/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=phys.au.dk|language=en}}</ref> Her research mainly covers the interaction between hydrogen atoms and carbon-based surfaces <ref>{{Cite web|last=|title=Surface physics - Surface Dynamics Group|url=https://phys.au.dk/forskning/forskningsomraader/condensed-matter-physics/surface-dynamics-group/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=phys.au.dk|language=en}}</ref>

In 2016, she won the prestigious [[EliteForsk Prize]], which was awarded by the [[Ministry of Higher Education and Science (Denmark)|Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2017 she was appointed Professor of Physics at Aarhus University as the first woman ever, and in 2020 she was elected as member of [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters|The Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pedersen|first=Lise Refstrup Linnebjerg|date=2020-10-08|title=The Interdisciplinary Nanoscience Center at Aarhus University: Liv Hornekær elected as member of The Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters|url=https://inano.au.dk/about/news-events/news/show/artikel/liv-hornekaer-elected-as-member-of-the-royal-danish-academy-of-sciences-and-letters/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=inano.au.dk|language=en}}</ref>
